claims.text: MJP French edition; Lazzaro via Maynard Asynchronous institutions

MJP’s 1832 French-edition crown instrument concerns Greece. Lazzaro’s 1876 Salonica report names an Ottoman governor-general and a Constantinople commission. These show asynchronous institutions, not simultaneous city transfer. The report’s prejudicial explanations of violence are excluded; no current sovereign title or universal consent follows.
Does the Greek crown instrument establish that Salonica had the same administration by 1876? The 1876 Salonica report still identifies Ottoman administrative officials
claims.address: model.PREDICTION; question and both options; answer relation

claims.text: What makes the two transitions asynchronous in the actual witnesses? The Greek crown instrument is 1832, while the 1876 Salonica report identifies Ottoman officials rather than the same Greek administration.

The 1832 Greek crown instrument does not imply the 1876 Salonica Ottoman administration changed simultaneously. Lazzaro’s report via Maynard is mediated evidence; prejudicial collective explanations, unchecked violence estimates and modern title claims are excluded.
